chapter_theme: Songs at Ratnagiri (இரத்னகிரி): the poet confesses he has lost goodness and sense to women's eyes, hair and breasts and to the five senses that cheat him toward death, and in a short song asks to sing the Thiruppugazh with devotion until he is freed; the praise names the vel against Sura and the jewel hill.
structure_note: Two songs of plea against women and the body (565, 566), the second with a long battle passage in drum syllables, and a short song of pure devotion (567).

565.reading: The poet says that through the kohl-dark eyes like carp that rival the doe, the dark hair like a fragrant swarming cloud and the breasts like golden pots, hills and caskets, he has lost goodness, knowledge and feeling, and asks how he will ever gain the good path. The praise names Murugan who struck down the mango-tree form in the dark sea and ended the gods' grief, the source of the three Tamils and of the meaning of japa, the true Kumara shining on Ratnagiri.
565.nuance: நலமற்று அறிவற்று உணர்வற்றனன்: the confession is a triple loss, goodness, knowledge and feeling, in one breath. கடலில் புகு கொக்கு: கொக்கு is the mango tree, and the line points to Sura hiding in the sea in that form, though the splitting of the line is not certain.

566.reading: The poet describes himself caught in a sorrowful household like a fish in a net, like straw fallen into gruel, his body like wax in a fire, a basket of impurity driven by the senses, while the five cheats of sound, touch, smell, form and taste play their falsehood as heedless Death draws near; he asks whether, seeking women's houses, he must stumble to his end in a body that stinks, and asks for the state that does not end. The praise is a battle dance in drum syllables in which Hari, Brahma, Siva and the goddess dance, Yama, foxes and ghouls feast as the vel is thrown, and names Murugan, lover of the doe-girl guarding the millet, at Ratnagiri.
566.nuance: சூதர் ஐவர் சத்த பரிசான மண ரூப ரசம்: the five senses are named as five gamblers or cheats, the five sense-objects listed in order. The similes for the trapped self (மீன் in the net, செத்தை in the gruel, மெழுகு in the fire) are piled one on another. சீசி இது நாற is the poet's own disgust at his body.

567.reading: A short song: the poet asks that, holding to Murugan with devotion and singing his great Thiruppugazh again and again, he become one freed and reach liberation. The praise names Murugan the best one, friend of the good who give, dweller on the peerless gem hill, the wise one who is the descent of the power of knowledge, the lord of the victorious vel.
567.nuance: The song names the book's own title (மா திருப்புகழ் பாடி) and makes singing it the way to mukti. ஞானசத்தி நிபாதா: சத்திநிபாதம், the descent of grace on a ripe soul, is a term of Saiva Siddhanta, here made a name of Murugan.
